resources.string: This program was developed to help people with school subjects, especially with foreign languages and biology.\n\nFor any further help contact me at litos@tuta.io

Every item is created from the floating New button at the bottom right. On the subjects screen it opens the subject creator right away; inside a container it fans out a circular palette of the offered types — drag the finger onto an icon, or tap the icon after a plain tap leaves the palette standing. A tap outside the icons closes the palette. 
The button hides when the list scrolls down and returns when it scrolls back up. 
All the creator dialogs have two columns for name of the new item and for its description (optional). 
The description of the item can be multiline. 
After you are done with these two colums, there can be more stuff for each different type of item. 
When you are done with all that information, click 'OK' to create the item, or click 'Cancel' to exit the dialog. A click outside the window closes the dialog too, but only when nothing was changed.
Notes carry a name and a description, and serve for any text that is not a word, like a grammar rule.
Below the fields sits an add icon, which adds a translate item. \nA translate consists of a name and an optional description. \nThe cancel icon on its right removes it.
This application has some more functions that can sometimes help. Here is the list and explanation of them.

If you have similar names of certain words, and they have identical translations, combine them using these: /(). \nSlash character signals two different options ending by a whitespace, an interpunction character or a bracket.
I/They come = \'I come\' or \'They come\' \n(I go)/(He goes). = \'I go.\' or \'He goes\'.

The menu shows Export only while rows are selected.
The export reaches every selected row except translations.
Word file: compact, no success rates, no references.
JSON file: complete, success rates, notes and references included.
Inside a subject the words land in it, at the subjects screen a new subject is created.\nAn error names the file and line. Fix that line and pick the file again.

Chapter: name { and } on their own lines.
Word: word = translation.
Note: = text.
Description: [text] after a name.
Variants: first\second.

Search finds names and translations in the open subject. 
The filter icon builds a query from labeled choices, so the prefix syntax stays optional. 
A word hit shows its translations directly, a settings toggle turns that off. 
A settings switch turns on diacritic-insensitive search.
Pick the type, what to compare and the condition, then enter a value. \nThe preview shows the written query before it runs. \nApply writes it into the field and starts the search.
The field accepts the written form the filter builds. \nA regular expression follows Java syntax.
\WR>50\t- words with success rate above 50% \n\sD\t- names starting with \'D\' \n\WD\hund\t- words whose description contains \'hund\'
Permanently deletes the selected items after accepting the delete-check dialog.

Only one item can be edited at a time. A window with parameters of the selected item pops up. The style of the editing window is same as when creating that type of item. \nClick the \'OK\' button to save the changes when done editing.

All created objects can be modified in some way. 
A long-press on an item starts the select mode: the item becomes selected and the bottom strip with possible actions shows. A tap on the type icon of a row toggles its selection too. 
Keep the finger pressed and move it over the list to select the range of items it crosses. 
While items are selected, the search button in the top right corner becomes the select-all toggle: it selects all items of the list, or (if all items are selected) exits the selection mode. The back key also exits the selection mode. 
The list of possible actions follows below.

Cuts all selected items and shows the paste sheet (cancel and paste buttons). After you open the target chapter, click \'Paste\'. \nThe armed move survives switching chapters, the side swipe included — the swipe only cancels the row selection.
The test asks for the words of the picked sources.

The report opens when you press 'Done' or the time runs out. 
The title shows the score of this test. 
Every row is one tested word. 
The large text is what the test asked: the translations, or the word in the reversed test. 
Below it are the correct answer and yours, green when right, red when wrong. 
The number with × counts how often the word was tested. 
The colour band runs from red to green with its overall success. 
The right end shows passed over tested. 
All counts already include this test. 
'Retake' runs a new test on the same sources.

'Start' needs at least one source. 
Each word is asked at most once, in a shuffled order. 
The countdown blinks red for the last 30 seconds. 
'Done' submits and asks first when answers are missing, a run-out time submits too. 
'QUIT' or the back button ends the run without grading after a confirmation.

The 'Add source' tile opens the picker, which browses like the explorer. 
'Select' on the strip adds the picked rows. 
A picked chapter stands for the words inside it. 
All sources must belong to one subject.

Every conflicting word needs a name

Each row is a word or a translation that reaches past the selection. 
A word row lives in containers outside the selection too, so the flip would change them. A translation row is shared with words outside, so the flip would copy it and the sharing would end. 
An untouched row keeps the relation, so everything it reaches outside joins the flip. The check runs again after every round, untouched rows can bring new ones. 
An edited row gives the flip a copy with the new contents, the outside keeps the original. 
A space behind the name is the invisible edit: the copy keeps the trimmed name and only the row detaches. 
The cross button drops the words of the row from the flip, nothing changes outside. 
A row left in the list without a name refuses the commit. When the list empties, the flip runs.
